basis: Clenching and tooth grinding define an oral parafunctional disorder; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis. Separate jaw disorders are not assumed.
Defined by full-thickness perforation of a gastric or duodenal ulcer.
Cerebral motor impairment causes spasticity of one limb; secondary muscle or joint damage is not established as defining or common.
Inflammation directly affects the intestinal pouch. Associated C. difficile colitis is a separate infection; inflammation alone does not establish an immune mechanism.
Mesothelial neoplasm arising in the peritoneal lining of the abdominal digestive compartment.
Inflammation directly affects renal tubules and interstitium; the umbrella includes multiple causes and does not uniformly establish an immune mechanism.
ID and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; damaging ocular anomalies and heart defects each 30-79%. Dental anomalies, often 80-99%, omitted for the cap in favor of more severe organ defects.

ID/microcephaly define disorder; nail hypoplasia and clinodactyly 2/2; delayed puberty 1/2 supports named hypogonadism. Ocular damage lacks frequency evidence; renal malrotation may not impair function.
Inherited epidermolysis bullosa subtype defined by skin cleavage and blistering; substantial extracutaneous damage is not established for this subtype.
Inherited susceptibility to persistent cutaneous HPV infection produces chronic skin lesions; immune abnormalities and recurrent skin infection occur in 80-99%.
Defined by failure of adrenal cortical hormone production; autoimmune causation is not universal across the umbrella.
Congenital absence of the spinal cord, classified as a neural tube defect; isolated concept does not establish other organ malformations.
Chronic Corynebacterium minutissimum infection directly affects skin folds.
Inherited retinal degeneration due to biallelic PCARE variants; no extraocular damage is established.
Primary nasal lymphoma occupies the nasal airway; lymphoid-cell neoplasia supports haematologic, and lymphoma requires infectious_immune.
Papillary urothelial neoplasm arises in the bladder, which belongs to the renal axis; future carcinoma is a separate risk.
Autoimmune myositis; swallowing dysfunction and sclerodactyly each 30-79% support gastrointestinal and skin involvement. Interstitial lung abnormalities are 5-29%; hypertension may be separate.
Defining vertebral/rib dysostosis and anal atresia; genitourinary malformations include urethral atresia and hydronephrosis. Pulmonary hypoplasia frequency is unspecified.
Carcinoma originates in the distal common bile duct; extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Germ-cell malignancy of the testis is reproductive, without defining endocrine dysfunction. Metastatic organ involvement is not established as common.
Glyoxylate metabolic defects cause oxalate excess; the represented primary hyperoxaluria phenotype commonly (>30%) causes damaging renal oxalate deposition.
Malignancy of the intracranial choroid plexus; vascular ancestry does not establish a primary blood-vessel malignancy or cardiovascular damage.
Bone-forming fibro-osseous neoplasm, typically of craniofacial bones; sinonasal or orbital proximity alone does not establish another damaged axis.
Defined by chronic axonal damage to peripheral sensory and motor nerves; weakness does not establish a separate primary muscle disorder.
Carcinoma originates in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes; epithelial origin alone does not make it a dermatologic disease.
